title: U.S. News: 26 ICE Custody Deaths in 7 Months, On Pace to Break All-Time Record
excerpt: An August 13, 2026, U.S. News & World Report investigation documented that 26 people had died in ICE custody or immediately after release through the first seven months of 2026, a pace that would exceed the prior-year total of 31 deaths — itself a two-decade high — by more than 25 percent.
content:
An investigative tracking report published by U.S. News & World Report on August 13, 2026, compiled official ICE death notifications and government data to quantify the accelerating toll of deaths in immigration detention.

  • With 26 reported deaths through the first seven months of 2026, the annual total was on pace to eclipse the prior year's figure by more than 25 percent.
  • The 31 deaths recorded in ICE custody in 2025 had already eclipsed the total number of deaths in ICE custody across the four prior years combined.
  • An investigation of Delaney Hall found contaminated food, extreme temperatures, and overcrowding at the facility, which had become a focal point of the crisis.

The report noted that amid the rising fatalities, ICE had reduced public reporting on detainee deaths. The agency had previously announced it would stop reporting deaths occurring soon after release from custody — a category created under the Biden administration to capture health deteriorations linked to detention conditions.
